metadata.title: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum in $115B stock deal

content.text:
This story was originally published on Manufacturing Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Manufacturing Dive newsletter.
Dive Brief:
-
Networking and artificial intelligence chipmaker Marvell Technology has agreed to buy Lumentum, a maker of optical components, in a $115 billion all-stock deal that includes Lumentum's debt.
-
The transaction represents about $1,132 per share of Lumentum common stock and a premium of about 23.9% based on each company's unaffected closing share price as of October 28, Marvell said in a news release.
-
After closing, current Marvell stockholders will own about 67% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, while Lumentum stockholders will own about 33%. The transaction will expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, Marvell said.
Dive Insight:
The data center construction boom is driving record demand and revenue for many technology companies, including Marvell and Lumentum.
According to Marvell, the artificial intelligence infrastructure industry has now reached "an inflection point" defined by rapidly growing bandwidth requirements, coupled with the physical limitations of copper-based wire. This is driving adoption of higher-bandwidth optical technologies to meet AI's increasing connectivity needs, the company said.
Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum joins "Marvell's strengths in electrical and optical interconnect, network switching, custom XPU [processors] and XPU attach and advanced semiconductor technologies with Lumentum's expertise in high-performance lasers, optical transceivers, optical circuit switching and specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing," per the news release.
"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Marvell Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy said in a statement. "By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value."
Murphy will serve as chairman and CEO of the combined company. The agreement, which Marvell said the boards of directors of both companies have unanimously approved, calls for Lumentum stockholders to receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each share of Lumentum common stock held at the time of closing.
According to market research firm TrendForce, the acquisition will "significantly strengthen Marvell's optical technology portfolio" and allow the company to produce "more comprehensive next-generation optical interconnect technology solutions." This could allow the combined company to compete more effectively with Broadcom, which dominates the optical interconnect market, TrendForce said.
